clue.text: Celebrity of European person showing up here

indicators.note: in a down entry, showing up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a man is a person

explanation.surface: Asks which famous European figure has turned up at this venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'showing up here' turns EMAN into NAME, since in a down light up means backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A big name is a famous person, so the word stands for a celebrity.

clue.text: Field hospital under pressure in dry setting

indicators.note: dry acts as a setting, the mount that holds the stones placed in it

parts.note: sere means dried up or withered

indicators.note: in a down entry, the letter placed under another comes after it

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure
H is the map abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A field hospital is set up in some arid desert location.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Field hospital' reads as one military unit, but Field is the definition; 'under' puts H below P, and 'setting' wraps SERE around them.
explanation.definitionFit: A sphere of activity is a field or area of interest, a common synonym.

clue.text: Pound invested in lesser bet — oddly, it's bound to make money

indicators.note: money invested in something is put inside it, so one letter goes inside the others
oddly signals the letters are arranged in a strange new order

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A gambler stakes a pound on a small wager, oddly certain to profit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' rearranges LESSER BET; 'invested in' puts L inside it. 'bound' is the clever twist: a book is bound.
explanation.definitionFit: A hit book sells in large numbers; a book is a bound volume, which makes the definition witty.

clue.text: Pair contracted fever in capital

parts.note: PR is the shortened form of pair
ague is a malarial fever with shivering

explanation.surface: Two travellers both caught a fever while visiting a capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contracted' looks like catching an illness, but it shortens Pair to PR.
explanation.definitionFit: This city is the capital of the Czech Republic.

clue.text: Male put on a garment nothing stops

parts.note: he is the male pronoun
a vest is an item of clothing
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A man dons a garment that nothing can stop.
explanation.walkthrough: A sailing term: a ship heaves to when it is brought to a halt facing the wind.
explanation.definitionFit: To heave to is the nautical phrase for halting a vessel, so it means stops.

clue.text: Top player suffering reverse at first as leading man

indicators.note: only the opening pair of letters of the word is turned round

parts.note: a star is a top performer

explanation.surface: A top sportsman suffers an early defeat while captaining the side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffering reverse at first' swaps the first two letters of STAR: ST becomes TS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Russian emperor was the leading man of his country, a ruler.

clue.text: Leading pairs eliminated from race came late — very grave situation

indicators.note: the first two letters of each of the next four words are dropped

explanation.surface: Front runners knocked out of a race that came in late: a very serious state of affairs.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping RA, CA, LA and VE leaves CE, ME, TE and RY. 'grave situation' is literal: where graves are situated.
explanation.definitionFit: A graveyard is where graves are situated, punning on grave meaning serious.

clue.text: Isolated state reduced, unfortunately

indicators.note: reduced means the word is cut down, losing letters from its end

parts.note: Alaska is the US state cut off from the rest of the mainland states

explanation.surface: An isolated nation has been diminished, sadly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' cuts KA from ALASKA, the US state separated from the others by Canada.
explanation.definitionFit: This interjection expresses regret, used like unfortunately or sadly.

clue.text: Short program about English fruit producer

parts.note: an applet is a small application program
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A brief broadcast on an English orchard grower.
explanation.definitionFit: This tree bears apples, so it is a producer of fruit.

clue.text: Spy chief taken in by deception, in a sense

indicators.note: one piece is held inside another, taken in by it

parts.note: a sell is a hoax or swindle
M is the head of the secret service in the James Bond stories

explanation.surface: The head of intelligence was fooled by a trick, in a way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in' suggests being fooled but puts M inside SELL, an old word for a hoax.
explanation.definitionFit: Detecting odours is one of the five senses, alongside sight and taste.

clue.text: Standing before court

parts.note: ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: Someone rises to their feet before the court.
explanation.definitionFit: Upright and standing are synonyms describing a vertical posture.

clue.text: Travel with author's son and private teacher

parts.note: go means travel
Jules Verne is the author, and his name takes the possessive

explanation.surface: A tutor goes on a journey with a writer's boy.
explanation.walkthrough: The author is Jules Verne, apt given his travel novels.
explanation.definitionFit: She was a woman employed to teach children at home, a private tutor.

clue.text: Interpreter of text, say, kept in college mostly

indicators.note: one piece is kept inside another, held within it
mostly means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: Exeter is a college of Oxford University
eg (for example) is signalled by say

explanation.surface: A translator of scripture, for example, held at a university college most of the time.
explanation.walkthrough: Exeter is an Oxford college; 'mostly' drops its last letter, and 'kept in' places 'say' inside what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a scholar explains or interprets a text, especially scripture.

clue.text: Page in some novel set in town, of course

indicators.note: one letter goes in among the others
novel means new, so the letters take a new order

explanation.surface: A page of some novel takes place in a town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' rearranges SOME to ESOM, with P inside. 'of course' points to a racecourse: Epsom hosts the Derby.
explanation.definitionFit: This Surrey town is home to the famous racecourse, so it is a town of racing.

clue.text: Organisations unknown in small parts of plant

indicators.note: the unknown letter is placed in the other letters

parts.note: stems are parts of a plant
Y is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: Groups that nobody knows about among small bits of plant life.
explanation.definitionFit: Structured setups and arrangements are organisations in the sense of ordered schemes.

clue.text: Suddenly put in the know, quietly call in child

indicators.note: the pieces go in the word for child, which surrounds them

parts.note: a son is a child
p (piano) is the musical direction for quietly
ring means telephone, call
up, as in clued up, means informed

explanation.surface: An informed person quietly phones about a child, a sudden revelation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the know' is clued up, informed; 'in' wraps the child round the other three pieces, in answer order rather than clue order.
explanation.definitionFit: To spring something upon someone is to present it suddenly, without warning.

clue.text: Not dry, like 10 of 27, regardless of 1

definitions.meaning: a wine that is not dry is sugary
Juliet says a rose by any other name would smell as this, so the smell of a rose, whatever its name

explanation.surface: A cross-reference riddle quoting Romeo and Juliet.
explanation.walkthrough: 10 is SMELL, 27 is ROSE and 1 is NAME: 'a rose by any other name would smell as sweet'.
explanation.definitionFit: Wine that is not dry is sugary; Shakespeare's line gives the second sense.

clue.text: Bit of a bloomer finishes off chess game — mate

indicators.note: finishes off picks the final letter of each word

parts.note: a pal is a mate, a friend

explanation.surface: Checkmate ends a chess game, ending it for a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' suggests a blunder in chess, but it means a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: This leaf-like part of a flower protects the bud, so it is part of a bloomer.

clue.text: See 24 across
Late genius that may prefix other solutions

definitions.meaning: Umberto, the Italian novelist who died in 2016, author of the novel at 24 across
a prefix meaning ecological, as in ecosystems

explanation.surface: A tribute to a recently dead thinker whose name starts other words.
explanation.walkthrough: The novelist Umberto wrote the novel at 24/18; 'other solutions' hints at eco-friendly answers.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian writer bore this surname, and the same letters form a prefix about the environment.

clue.text: Flaws in conclusions from some idiotic ass without sound reflection

indicators.note: the flaws go in among the end letters
conclusions are the final letters of each word

parts.note: holes are flaws, as in an argument

explanation.surface: Faults in an idiot's conclusions, made without any sound reasoning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound reflection' suggests sound thinking, but it is an echo bouncing back.
explanation.definitionFit: A room lacking any echo has no sound reflected back, so no reverberation.

clue.text: What poets generally do, Keats and Yeats don't

definitions.meaning: poets usually write verse with matching end sounds
the two names look alike but are not pronounced alike: Yeats says YATES

explanation.surface: A paradox about two famous poets.
explanation.walkthrough: Keats and Yeats look as if they match but Yeats is pronounced 'Yates'.
explanation.definitionFit: Matching end sounds are a staple of verse, and these two names lack that match.

clue.text: National leader performing in moving protest

indicators.note: one piece goes in the other

parts.note: a march is a protest on the move
on means on stage, performing

explanation.surface: A head of state takes part in a protest march.
explanation.definitionFit: A king or queen is the sovereign heading a nation.

clue.text: Part of grounds and pitch where kids can play

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Describes a section of the playing fields set aside for children.
explanation.definitionFit: A box of sand is a play area for small children in parks and gardens.

clue.text: Notice about South American oil source

indicators.note: about means surrounding, going round the other pieces

parts.note: see means notice

explanation.surface: An announcement concerning oil from South America.
explanation.definitionFit: The seeds of this plant are pressed to give a cooking oil.

clue.text: Piano I installed in disorderly club open to all

indicators.note: the letter is installed inside the others
disorderly means the letters are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: A piano is put into a rowdy nightclub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disorderly' turns CLUB into UBLC, and 'installed in' puts I before its C.
explanation.definitionFit: Something accessible to everyone is open to all rather than private.

clue.text: Ruined couple's mutual fund — that shows effect of world revolution

definitions.text: that shows effect of world revolution

indicators.note: ruined means wrecked, so the letters are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A couple's shared savings have been wiped out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'world revolution' sounds political but means the earth's rotation, which this swinging device demonstrates.
explanation.definitionFit: This swinging weight's plane slowly turns, demonstrating the earth's rotation.

clue.text: Fellow scoffed a lot

parts.note: scoffed means ate greedily

explanation.surface: A man wolfed down a great deal of food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot' looks like quantity, but lot means destiny.
explanation.definitionFit: One's lot in life is one's destiny.

clue.text: Primate set over south part of church

indicators.note: the primate is set over, covering, the south letter

parts.note: an ape is a primate

explanation.surface: A monkey is placed above the southern section of a church.
explanation.definitionFit: The semicircular end of a church, usually behind the altar.

clue.text: Except for its head, river is brown

indicators.note: the river's name is used without its first letter

parts.note: the Humber is a river estuary in north-east England

explanation.surface: A river that is brown apart from its source.
explanation.walkthrough: The Humber is an estuary in north-east England; dropping its head H leaves the pigment.
explanation.definitionFit: This natural earth pigment gives a dark brown colour.

clue.text: Pink was revolting

definitions.meaning: a pinkish red shade, as in the flower colour

explanation.surface: A colour that was disgusting.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a pink shade and is also the past tense of rise, to rebel.

clue.text: Travels round city on Loire

definitions.meaning: goes on trips around a place
the French city on the river Loire

explanation.surface: Journeys around a French city.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means trips around somewhere and is also a French city on the Loire.

clue.text: Languages such as Hebrew, including old study of signs

indicators.note: including means the first piece takes in the second

parts.note: Semitics refers to the Semitic languages, including Hebrew and Arabic

explanation.surface: Hebrew and similar tongues, including old ones.
explanation.definitionFit: This discipline studies signs and symbols and how meaning is made.
